primitives.title: Agents and objectives
questions: What objective is observed versus assumed?

primitives.title: Property, control and enforcement
questions: Who owns, controls, can exclude, or bears liability?

primitives.title: Information and uncertainty
questions: Who knows what, when, and at what cost?

primitives.title: Time, money and credit
questions: How are obligations settled across time?
What creates liquidity or maturity mismatch?

primitives.title: Institutions and rules
questions: How are rules enforced and changed?

primitives.title: Networks and geography
questions: Which relationships, routes, clusters and distances constrain activity?

mechanisms.title: Marginal trade-off
mechanisms.test: Observe responses to a change in the binding constraint.

mechanisms.title: Specialization and coordination
mechanisms.test: Compare coordination and production costs across organizational forms.

mechanisms.title: Price formation and bargaining
mechanisms.test: Compare bids, accepted transactions, failed matches and bargaining outcomes.

mechanisms.title: Credit creation and balance-sheet expansion
mechanisms.test: Reconcile assets, liabilities, collateral, cash flows and settlement.

mechanisms.title: Market power and entry
mechanisms.test: Study margins, concentration, entry, exit, switching and capacity.

mechanisms.title: External costs and public goods
mechanisms.test: Identify affected parties, counterfactuals and who pays.

mechanisms.title: Risk transfer and liquidity
mechanisms.test: Compare promised payoff, collateral, liquidity and realized loss.

model_families.title: Double-entry and stock-flow consistency
assumptions: relevant sectors and counterparties are represented
failure_questions: Are valuation changes confused with transactions?

model_families.title: Strategic interaction
assumptions: players, actions, payoffs and information are explicit

model_families.title: Dynamic stochastic systems
assumptions: state variables and transition process are specified

model_families.title: Causal inference
assumptions: estimand and identification strategy are explicit
failure_questions: Do assumptions survive institutional and temporal changes?

research_rules: Never equate accounting identity with causal explanation.
Never equate equilibrium with observed market clearing.
Never treat a forecast as a fact.
Require a counterexample search for every promoted general claim.
Preserve original data vintages and the information set available at forecast time.
Compare competing model families using common observations and explicit assumptions.
Mark novel hypotheses as candidate until independently tested.
